title: Seeking the Magic Mushroom
author: R. Gordon Wasson
summary: R. Gordon Wasson's photo-essay in Life magazine announcing that he and photographer Allan Richardson had participated in a Mazatec mushroom ceremony near Huautla de Jiménez in June 1955. The article, illustrated with color photographs and watercolor plates, named Roger Heim as Wasson's collaborator.
excerpt: "Richardson and I were the first white men in recorded history to eat the divine mushrooms, which for centuries have been a secret of certain Indian peoples living far from the great world in southern Mexico. No anthropologists had ever described the scene that we witnessed."
citation: Wasson, R. Gordon. "Seeking the Magic Mushroom." Life, May 13, 1957, 100-102, 109-120.

draft.rationale: The single most consequential popularization in the archive's rediscovery arc: a mass-circulation magazine piece that moved the Mazatec mushroom cult from specialist ethnobotany into American popular consciousness. It effectively launched the postwar Western psilocybin vogue and was the direct trigger for Hofmann's 1958 isolation of psilocybin and the wave of self-experimentation that followed through the early 1960s.
